column6: One sentence says what the project is and for whom, the problem is stated in the user's terms, and no course vocabulary (capstone, team, partner, sprint, rubric) appears on the page.
column9: The description is understandable but generic, the problem is stated in the team's terms rather than the user's, or course vocabulary appears on the page.
column12: A visitor cannot tell what the project is or who it is for.

column6: Three to five highlights written from the audience's perspective, at least one real visual of the project actually running, and a call to action that works.
column9: Highlights are present but feature-listy rather than audience-facing, the visual is a mockup or placeholder, or the call to action is unclear.
column12: No highlights, no real visual of the project, or no way to access it.

column6: Every team member credited, past contributors acknowledged where applicable, and a working feedback or contact channel.
column9: Credits present but incomplete, or a contact channel is named without being usable.

column6: Intentional visual hierarchy, alt text on every meaningful image, sufficient color contrast, descriptive link text, and nothing broken.
column9: The page is presentable but has accessibility gaps: missing alt text, low contrast, or "click here" link text.
column12: Visibly unfinished, or accessibility problems that block use.
